summary: Phase 4 Slice G (packet-sharing routes — POST /api/packets/share, GET /api/packets/{token}, GET /api/packets/{token}/document/{doc_id}, POST /api/packets/{token}/sign/{doc_id}) verified GREEN end-to-end. Backend pytest: 33/33 PASS in test_iteration16_phase4g_packets_dualwrite.py. (1) POST /api/packets/share (admin) dual-writes — Postgres row has recipient_name='TEST_SliceG_Create', recipient_role='caregiver', category='caregiver_onboarding', viewed_at NULL, completed_at NULL, signed_ids empty, created_by=ADMIN_UUID; Mongo mirror identical. Caregiver POST /packets/share returns 403; unauthenticated returns 401/403. (2) GET /api/packets/{token} (public, no auth) reads packet metadata from Postgres and documents list from Mongo (no file_base64 leaked, sorted by seq ascending 1..14 for caregiver_onboarding). First view flips viewed_at from NULL to ISO timestamp in BOTH stores; second view does NOT overwrite (PG viewed_at preserved across calls, Mongo viewed_at preserved across calls). Unknown token returns 404. (3) GET /api/packets/{token}/document/{doc_id} returns application/pdf, body starts with %PDF and contains %%EOF (stamped overlay with recipient_name + UTC timestamp); unknown token => 404; unknown doc_id => 404. (4) POST /api/packets/{token}/sign/{doc_id} with valid base64 PNG dual-writes signed Document: Postgres documents row exists (category=caregiver_onboarding, mime_type=application/pdf, storage_path='documents/<signed_id>.pdf', owner_id=NULL, uploaded_by=NULL — both deliberately nulled because Mongo values 'packet-token' and 'public-share' are non-UUID); Mongo documents row exists (owner_id=token, uploaded_by='public-share'); Supabase Storage bucket 'documents' contains <signed_id>.pdf (verified via service-role list). signed_ids array updated in BOTH Postgres ($2::uuid conditional append) and Mongo ($addToSet). (5) Completion gate: signing 1 of 14 docs leaves completed_at NULL in BOTH stores (verified explicitly — does NOT flip prematurely). (6) Idempotency: signing the same doc twice creates two separate signed Document rows (one per call) but signed_ids in BOTH stores contains doc_id exactly once (PG conditional-append + Mongo $addToSet both idempotent). (7) Invalid signature_base64 ('' empty) => 400; unknown token on sign => 404; unknown doc_id on sign => 404. (8) Phase 4 Slice A/B/C/D/E/F regression GREEN under BOTH legacy HS256 (Admin@123) and Supabase ES256 (AdminPassword123!) JWTs across 9 endpoints (auth/me, caregivers, clients list+detail, assignments, documents, shifts, chat/threads, chat/contacts, onboarding?caregiver_id=<demo>) — 18 parametrised tests all pass. (9) Final parity exact: PG packet_shares=2 == Mongo packet_shares=2; PG documents=50 == Mongo documents=50 (matches the baseline in /app/memory/test_credentials.md). All test_signed_doc_ids, _packet_tokens, _storage_paths tracked and removed via module-end fixture; verified via direct asyncpg/motor probes after the run. Frontend regression (Expo web, mobile 390x844): admin login (Supabase mode) -> Documents tab -> 'Share Packet' modal opens -> selects Caregiver (14) category -> recipient name 'UI Test Caregiver' -> Generate link -> link reveals as https://.../packet/<token> and the Open preview/Copy controls render. Public viewer (/packet/<token>) initially threw a red-screen ReferenceError 'PdfViewerModal is not defined' at app/packet/[token].tsx:138 — FIXED by adding the missing `import { PdfViewerModal } from '@/src/components/pdf/PdfViewerModal'` (line 13). After `sudo supervisorctl restart expo` the public viewer renders the brand header, 'Welcome, UI Public Viewer Final', '0 of 14 signed' progress, and 14 numbered rows (01 Employment Application … 14) each with view + sign buttons (data-testid packet-doc-<id> and packet-sign-<id>). Smoke script /app/scripts/_smoke_slice_g.py PASSES. No expo deprecated packages introduced by Slice G.

ui_bugs.issue: Public packet viewer threw 'ReferenceError: PdfViewerModal is not defined' at line 138 because the component was used but not imported. FIXED by adding `import { PdfViewerModal } from '@/src/components/pdf/PdfViewerModal'`. After expo restart, the public viewer renders correctly (Welcome header + 14 doc rows + progress bar).

action_items: (Optional) Slice J Mongo decommission: GET /api/packets/{token} still pulls the documents list from Mongo (`db.documents.find({category}).sort('seq')`). When the Mongo cutover happens, switch this to Postgres `select * from public.documents where category=$1 order by seq` and the route becomes fully PG-sourced.

(Optional) supa_data.upsert_packet uses `on conflict (id) do update set viewed_at, completed_at, signed_ids` — recipient_name/role/category/email/phone are NOT in the conflict-update list. That's correct for share-creation (insert-only path) but means if the same packet id is ever re-upserted the recipient metadata silently stays stale. Not a Slice G regression.

(Optional) Backend log noise: ImageReader at /app/backend/server.py:1424 logs 'broken data stream' when the signed PNG is the 1x1 test image (the canvas drawImage still runs but the image is too small to render meaningfully). Wrap the log in `logger.warning` instead of `error`, or skip drawing when image bytes < 64. Not a functional bug — the signed PDF is still produced with the timestamp/name strings.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1308-1344 share_packet — writes Mongo first then PG via supa_data.upsert_packet. supa_data._safe swallows PG errors, so if Mongo writes and PG fails the client receives 200 with no drift signal. Same pattern as Slice F; acceptable until Slice J makes PG authoritative.

server.py:1347-1364 get_packet — reads packet metadata from PG (`supa_data.get_packet_by_token`) but the documents list is still pulled from Mongo (`db.documents.find({category}).sort('seq')`). This means a divergence in Mongo documents would still surface to public packet viewers. For Slice G this is the documented behaviour (per request 'docs list still from Mongo'), but should be migrated in Slice J.

server.py:1394 packet_sign — reads the packet from MONGO (`db.packet_shares.find_one`) not PG. So if Mongo packet_shares drifts away from PG, signing would 404 incorrectly. Tolerable while dual-write invariants hold; recommended switch to `supa_data.get_packet_by_token` once authoritative source is PG.

server.py:1467-1470 — Mongo uses $addToSet (idempotent) and PG uses conditional case-when (idempotent). Both verified by test_sign_same_doc_twice_idempotent_in_pg. Note: signing the SAME doc twice still creates TWO separate signed Document rows (one per call) — each gets its own UUID and storage object. That is by design (each signature attempt produces a new immutable artifact); not a duplicate-key bug.

server.py:1471-1479 completion gate — counts all docs in `category` (currently 14 for caregiver_onboarding) and flips completed_at only when signed_ids.length >= total. Verified to NOT prematurely complete when only 1 of 14 are signed.
supa_data.py:932-941 packet_add_signed_id — case statement `when $2::uuid = any(signed_ids) then signed_ids else signed_ids || $2::uuid end` is correct PG idiom for conditional append.
supa_data.py:923-929 mark_packet_viewed — `set viewed_at = coalesce(viewed_at, $2)` correctly preserves first-view timestamp on subsequent calls. Verified.

app/packet/[token].tsx — Missing import of PdfViewerModal caused a red-screen. Fixed during test run. The fetch on line 37 uses no auth headers (correct — it's a public endpoint). Loading state is shown via ActivityIndicator (good UX). The signature canvas at line 9 (`react-native-signature-canvas`) is a web-supported lib.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 4 Slice G is GREEN. All packet-sharing endpoints are dual-write: POST /packets/share writes Mongo then PG via supa_data.upsert_packet; GET /packets/{token} reads metadata from PG (supa_data.get_packet_by_token) but docs list still from Mongo (per Slice G scope, deferred to Slice J); GET /packets/{token}/document/{doc_id} reads PDF bytes from Mongo (unchanged from prior slices); POST /packets/{token}/sign dual-writes signed Document to Mongo + PG + Supabase Storage and dual-updates signed_ids via $addToSet (Mongo) + conditional case-when append (PG). Signed Document's owner_id and uploaded_by are NULLed in PG only (because Mongo stores them as 'packet-token' string and 'public-share' which fail PG's UUID FK). Completion gate counts category-wide documents and only flips completed_at when ALL are signed (the standard 14-doc caregiver_onboarding packet means signing 1 leaves completed_at=NULL). Reusable fixtures in test_iteration16_phase4g_packets_dualwrite.py: legacy_admin_token, supabase_admin_token, legacy_caregiver_token, HA/HCG/HSUPA headers; pg_fetchrow/pg_fetchval/pg_execute/pg_fetch + mongo_count/mongo_find_one/mongo_delete sync wrappers; module-scope autouse _cleanup_at_end that removes tracked _packet_tokens, _signed_doc_ids, _storage_paths from all three stores. Front-end testIDs verified: share-packet-button (documents tab), share-cat-caregiver_onboarding, share-name-input, share-email-input, share-generate-btn, share-link-copy, share-open-btn (Documents tab Share modal); packet-doc-<id>, packet-sign-<id> (public viewer rows). The next slice (per /app/scripts/) is Slice H or Slice J (Mongo decommission of the get_packet docs read + the packet_sign Mongo packet lookup).
rca_of_issue: One frontend red-screen bug discovered and fixed: /app/frontend/app/packet/[token].tsx referenced PdfViewerModal at line 138 without importing it, throwing 'ReferenceError: PdfViewerModal is not defined' on the public packet viewer route. Repro: any recipient opening the shared /packet/<token> URL would see the Expo error screen instead of the packet documents. Cause: the import was added to other consumers (documents.tsx, client/[id].tsx, caregiver/[id].tsx, policies.tsx) but missed in packet/[token].tsx during Slice G frontend changes. Fix: added `import { PdfViewerModal } from '@/src/components/pdf/PdfViewerModal'` to the imports block (line 13). After `sudo supervisorctl restart expo` the route renders correctly. No backend changes were required — Slice G backend is fully functional as designed; this was purely a missing-import on the existing Slice C public viewer that was not touched again until the Slice G end-to-end test.
